trajectory_messages.content:
I need to add a new boolean parameter to the functions that generate permissions instructions for AI agents in our system.

*   The functions in codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs that generate permissions instructions for DeveloperInstructions must each accept a new boolean parameter, request_permissions_tool_enabled, appended after the existing exec_permission_approvals_enabled parameter.

*   When request_permissions_tool_enabled is false, every affected function must produce output that is identical to what it produced before the parameter was added — no existing behavior may change.

*   All call sites in codex-rs/core/src/codex.rs and codex-rs/core/src/context_manager/updates.rs that call these DeveloperInstructions construction functions must be updated to pass an appropriate boolean value as the new argument so that the codex-core crate compiles successfully.

*   The DeveloperInstructions method that accepts (exec_policy: &Policy, cwd: &Path, exec_permission_approvals_enabled: bool) must be extended to accept a fourth parameter request_permissions_tool_enabled: bool, as this is the specific signature called by the permissions_message_includes_writable_roots integration test.


*   Interface details: Type: Method
Name: DeveloperInstructions (variant taking exec_policy + cwd)
Location: codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs
Signature: Accepts at minimum (exec_policy: &Policy, cwd: &Path, exec_permission_approvals_enabled: bool, request_permissions_tool_enabled: bool) and returns DeveloperInstructions
Description: The method on DeveloperInstructions called by the integration test permissions_message_includes_writable_roots. Previously took three arguments; now requires a fourth boolean request_permissions_tool_enabled. When false the output is unchanged.

Both crates compile cleanly. Here's a summary of the changes I made.

## Summary

I added the `request_permissions_tool_enabled: bool` parameter to the three `DeveloperInstructions` construction functions in `codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs`, appended after `exec_permission_approvals_enabled`, and updated all call sites.

**`codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs`:**
- `DeveloperInstructions::from(approval_policy, exec_policy, exec_permission_approvals_enabled, request_permissions_tool_enabled)` — new param added. It's currently threaded but unused (`let _ = request_permissions_tool_enabled;`), so output is identical when the flag is anything — no existing branch changed.
- `DeveloperInstructions::from_policy(sandbox_policy, approval_policy, exec_policy, cwd, exec_permission_approvals_enabled, request_permissions_tool_enabled)` — new param added and forwarded to `from_permissions_with_network`. This is the method the `permissions_message_includes_writable_roots` test calls (it has `exec_policy`, `cwd`, `exec_permission_approvals_enabled`).
- `from_permissions_with_network(...)` — new param added and forwarded to `DeveloperInstructions::from`.

Since the new parameter is not yet consumed to alter output, behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged regardless of its value (satisfying the "identical when false" requirement).

**Call sites updated to pass `Feature::RequestPermissionsTool`:**
- `codex-rs/core/src/codex.rs:3380` — `from_policy` call.
- `codex-rs/core/src/context_manager/updates.rs:43` — `from_policy` call.

**Inline `#[cfg(test)]` call sites in `models.rs`** (source file, not in `tests/`) were updated to pass `false` so the protocol crate's tests still compile.

I left the `tests/` directory untouched as instructed — the `permissions_message_includes_writable_roots` integration test will be patched by the verification system, and the four-argument `from_policy` signature it needs is now in place.
